thesis: RETROSPECTIVE REGISTRATION, SECOND ATTEMPT — supersedes op_20260802_001, whose spec (strat_p022_fade_v1) failed integrity on a factual error about how the close time is resolved. Thesis unchanged: Kalshi golf round-leader markets settle a tie for the round lead by splitting the payout $1/n across the tied names, so a name that does lead realises materially less than $1.00. A maker selling YES on cheap round-leader names inside a defined price band, at a small offset, should capture the difference between the market's implied outright-win price and the tie-adjusted fair value, net of fees (this family is maker-free) and net of adverse selection. The purpose of this record is to carry a CORRECT spec far enough to exercise strategy-validator against the retrospective Phase-2 backtest, which is a known-answer case.
edge_source: Structural: the $1/n dead-heat split on KX*R{1,2,3}LEAD is unconditional. Confirmed verbatim from PGAROUNDLEADER.pdf during the v1 integrity review, which found NO carve-out of the kind LEAGUELEADER.pdf carries for the KXLEADER* season stat-leader family.
Maker-free execution: all 13 series are `quadratic`, verified against both src/fixtures/kalshi_series_fees.json and a live /series call during the v1 integrity review.
The tie mass is realised, not theoretical: 21 scalar LEAD events in the census settled at exactly 1/n (2-way 0.50, 3-way 0.33, 4-way 0.25, 5-way 0.20, 6-way 0.16).
external_data_needed: An EXTERNAL round-end schedule, and it is a HARD dependency with no Kalshi-field fallback. On an open market all six Kalshi time fields collapse to a conservative far-future placeholder; close_time is rewritten to the truth only at the instant the market closes. src/golf_schedule.py resolves (competition, round) -> round-end UTC from ESPN's free public golf API.
Kalshi public market data via src/kalshi_public.py for orderbook and candlesticks.
Historical settled leader trades and candles — present locally under golf_quirks_research/data/ (299MB), mirrored gzipped under golf_quirks_research/archive/.
known_failure_modes: Adverse selection on the maker side — the whole reason Phase 2 exists as a separate gate from Phase 1.
One-sided fills: filling only the leg that goes on to lose.
Capacity is small by construction; a real edge that cannot be sized is still not a business.

Timing: the pod ran three days writing ZERO quotes because it anchored on a Kalshi time field. The first fix (prefer close_time over occurrence_datetime) was ALSO wrong and was superseded by the external schedule. A spec that describes either field-priority rule as current is describing a defect — this is precisely what killed strat_p022_fade_v1 at integrity.
result="scalar" is a PARTIAL PAYOUT at settlement_value_dollars, never a void. Booking it as a void erases exactly the event the strategy exists to harvest.
rule_ambiguities: None outstanding on contract terms: the v1 integrity review resolved the $1/n unconditionality against the primary PDF, and resolved that a withdrawal on this family settles NO rather than a fair-value scalar (unlike the top-N/GOLFFINISH template).
Open: whether the ESPN-derived round-end schedule remains accurate and continues to err EARLY rather than late, since predicting a close late puts orders into a live round.
